title: Indian Seafarer Injured as Projectile Hits Tanker in Persian Gulf
excerpt: Four crew were injured on the Liberia-flagged MT Fujairah Energy on November 10, including one Indian taken ashore with minor injuries; the other five Indians on board are safe, Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said.
body:
• The Liberia-flagged VLCC MT Fujairah Energy was hit by an unidentified projectile on November 10 while sailing from Al Ruwais to Dubai through the Persian Gulf, Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said.
  • Four crew members were injured in total. One of them is an Indian national who suffered minor injuries and was taken ashore for further medical examination.
  • Six Indian seafarers were on board. The remaining 18 crew members, including the other five Indians, are safe and accounted for, according to the minister.
  • For families of Indian seafarers in the Gulf: the government says it is monitoring the situation continuously and is in close contact with the ship management company on security, medical care and wellbeing - no attacker has been identified in these reports.

Four crew members were injured when a Liberia-flagged supertanker carrying six Indian seafarers was struck by an unidentified projectile in the Persian Gulf on November 10, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said in a post on X.

The vessel, the very large crude carrier MT Fujairah Energy, was travelling from Al Ruwais to Dubai when it was hit, according to Sonowal. One Indian national was among the four injured. He suffered minor injuries and was safely taken ashore for further medical examination, the minister said.

"Four crew members sustained injuries in the attack, including one Indian national, who suffered minor injuries and has been safely taken ashore for further medical examination. The remaining 18 crew members, including the other 5 Indian seafarers, are safe and accounted for."

- Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways, on X

What the government is doing

Sonowal added that the government is continuously monitoring the situation and remains in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security, medical care and wellbeing of the seafarers, in statements carried by ANI and IANS. The reports do not name the ship management company, do not describe damage to the vessel, and do not attribute the projectile to any country or group.

Separate Gulf incidents reported the same day

One report, in The Indian Messenger, also described two related maritime developments, and they should not be conflated with the Fujairah Energy strike. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said early on November 11 that it had received a report of a security incident involving a commercial tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, with crew, damage and environmental details still under assessment, and advised vessels to exercise extreme caution. Separately, ADNOC Logistics and Services confirmed one of its vessels sustained damage in an attack in UAE territorial waters in the Arabian Gulf on November 10, without identifying the vessel. Neither report identifies those vessels as the Fujairah Energy.

Why Indian seafarers are exposed

The incident lands against a count the Ministry of External Affairs gave last week. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on November 3 that India had lost 23 nationals in the ongoing conflict in West Asia, including 15 Indian seafarers, according to ANI reporting carried by Devdiscourse and IANS. Jaiswal also described a separate attack off Oman in which an Indian seafarer was killed and 13 other Indian crew members were rescued, with repatriation being arranged.

India supplies a large share of the world's merchant-navy crews, which is why a single projectile in the Gulf quickly becomes a consular and family story across coastal India. For now, the confirmed facts on this vessel are narrow: one Indian injured, described as minor; five other Indians safe; and a government statement that monitoring and contact with the ship's managers are continuing. Further official updates would be expected from the Shipping Ministry and the MEA.
nri_angle: Six Indians were crewing the tanker; one was injured and taken ashore, five are safe, and New Delhi says it is in close contact with the ship management company.
